Subject: Galileotech POC: procurement routing & payment path — recap and next steps

Hi Maya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good discussion on the POC scope and the success metrics you care about (99th-pct latency under 150ms, embedding throughput for batch similarity). Per our notes, I wanted to capture the procurement/payment options and proposed next steps so we can avoid surprises during vendor setup.

Summary of what we discussed:
- POC run length: 6 weeks, small pilot team (5 engineers), expected spend ~$8k-$12k for first month.
- Preferred production purchase: PO for annual contract (AP requires a vendor profile).
- For POC: you asked whether a corporate card could be used to accelerate onboarding.
- Marketplace: you said procurement is open to using cloud marketplace if Redwood is listed (saves internal vendor onboarding).

Immediate asks for AP team to confirm:
1) Is a corporate card acceptable for a one-time POC charge up to ~$15k?
2) If not, what's their lead time to issue a PO and complete vendor onboarding (W-9, tax forms, bank details)?
3) Any marketplace partners you prefer we route through?

Attachments: SOW-draft.pdf (outline of POC deliverables).

Next steps (my proposed plan):
- If card OK for POC, we run the 6-week pilot and convert to PO for production.
- If card is blocked, we'll work with your AP owner to fast-track vendor setup; we can provide all onboarding docs in one package.

I copied a brief pricing summary as an attachment for AP review. Happy to hop on a short call with AP if that helps.

Thanks —
Ben Carter

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from my side and Ive looped AP so they can chime in with exact timelines: 

1) Card for POC: In general we prefer POs for vendor spend, but AP makes exceptions for quick pilots under $10k. 
2) Vendor onboarding: Standard process is ~10 business days once we have the W-9, bank details, and a copy of the SOW. Theres occasionally speed-ups but AP would need the completed packet.
3) Marketplace: Were interested in marketplace billing (reduces internal approvals) — please confirm whether Redwood is currently listed (or planning to be).

If we want to use card for the first month, AP has a form to pre-authorize one-off card payments; Ill forward that. Also, I attached the contact for our procurement lead (in AP) who will handle vendor setup.

Forwarding the exchange with Maya. AP is leaning toward POs for production but may allow a one-off card for a small POC. Two internal asks:

1) Pricing concession: can we offer a one-month promotional credit (10-15%) if they commit to a 12-month PO after the POC? If legal/pricing is OK, that makes the PO path much easier for procurement to justify.
2) Quick onboarding bundle: Id like to send AP a single ZIP of all onboarding docs (W-9, insurance cert, PO template, contact list) and offer a 30-minute "vendor setup" call to get them across the finish line.

Proposed routing:
- Option A (fast): approve card payment up to $12k for POC; run pilot; convert to PO for prod.

Subject: Re: Galileotech POC: procurement routing & payment path — recap and next steps

Hi Ben / Maya,

Thanks for the summary. A few AP clarifications so we have a clean path: 

- Vendor onboarding checklist we require: completed W-9, corporate ACH details, Certificate of Insurance (if >$25k/year), copy of executed SOW/contract. Once we have these, onboarding is typically 7-10 business days.
- Card payments: AP can approve one-off card transactions only up to $10,000 without director-level sign-off. Anything above requires a PO.
- Marketplace: If Redwood is a listed partner on our cloud marketplace and bills through that channel, we can bypass vendor onboarding. Please provide marketplace listing details if available.

We do accept DocuSign for SOW execution. Please submit SOW and W-9 to ap@galileotech.com and well start the vendor profile.

Regards,
AP Team
Galileotech
